newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady despite lower reserves.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady despite lower reserves.

text.p: German call money rates remained relatively stable on Monday despite a signigicant fall in reserve levels.
Traders said call money was trading at around 3.05 to 3.08 percent in quiet mid-morning trade, broadly unchanged from Friday 3.05 to 3.07 percent levels.
They said most market players were evidently confident that liquidity levels would increase in the coming sessions.
"Rates ticked up a bit earlier when the tight reserve figures came out, but now they have come off again," said one trader in Frankfurt.

The Bundesbank said earlier that funds held in reserve by commercial banks dropped to 38.7 billion marks on Friday from 41.4 on Wednesday. German financial markets were closed last Thursday for the Ascension Day bank holiday.
The monthly average for reserves held at the central bank also sank, down at 39.9 billion marks from 40.3 billion on Wednesday.

Borrowing on the 4.50 percent emergency Lombard facility was negligible and the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was quoted at 3.09633 percent on Monday, up slightly from Friday 3.09100 percent.
